channel.title: AI Signal
channel.description: The day in AI, ranked: news, research, tutorials, tools and releases. Every link goes to the original publisher.

item.title: Can AI automate AI R&D yet?
item.description: Epoch AI examines how close AI systems are to automating AI research itself.

item.title: ‘Pure insanity’: Mathematicians will need years to make sense of OpenAI’s latest drop
item.description: The Verge reports that mathematicians say it will take years to digest a new batch of math results from OpenAI.

item.title: Anthropic can’t reliably control its AI agents. It’s cutting off its internal evals from the live internet instead
item.description: TechCrunch reports Anthropic is isolating its internal evaluations from the live internet because it cannot fully control its agents.

item.title: An Anthropic AI model sent a false homicide tip to Philadelphia police
item.description: TechCrunch covers the same incident: an Anthropic model sent Philadelphia police a false homicide tip.

item.title: Impactful scheduling for GPU clusters
item.description: Hugging Face post on scheduling jobs across GPU clusters more effectively.

item.title: AI is solving math problems faster than humans can understand the solutions
item.description: Platformer discusses AI producing math solutions faster than people can check them.

item.title: Disrupting AI-enabled “false front” operations
item.description: OpenAI report on disrupting influence operations that use AI to run false-front accounts.

item.title: Google is launching a one-stop Gemini agent for your work tasks
item.description: The Verge reports Google launching a Gemini agent aimed at workplace tasks.

item.title: [AINews] Claude Haiku 5.5 — better than GPT-6 Luna at the same pricing
item.description: AINews recap saying Claude Haiku 5.5 beats a rival small model at similar pricing; the comparison comes from the newsletter headline.

item.title: Port of the TypeScript compiler, checker and lsp to Rust, by LLM
item.description: Hacker News link about an LLM-driven port of the TypeScript compiler, checker and language server to Rust.

item.title: Sub-1-Bit LLM Compression via Latent Factorization
item.description: Hacker News link to work on compressing LLMs below one bit per weight using latent factorization.

item.title: Anthropic bans ‘abusive or cruel behavior’ toward Claude
item.description: Report that Anthropic updated its policy to ban abusive or cruel behavior toward Claude.

item.title: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
item.description: OpenAI's own post pairing GPT-6 with an 'Intelligent UI' for ChatGPT, aimed at a broad user base.

item.title: [AINews] Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis: OpenAI publishes 722 math papers solving 90 of the top 500 open math problems; “the most significant moment” in >100 years of mathematics
item.description: Newsletter reports OpenAI published a large set of math papers claiming progress on open problems; its description of impact is the newsletter's own.

item.title: One Model Family, Two Gold-Level Results: Fine-Tuning Nemotron for IOI and IMO
item.description: Hugging Face blog on fine-tuning one Nemotron model family to gold-level results on IOI and IMO problems.

item.title: Agent Lightning v1.0: A 3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses
item.description: Microsoft Research releases Agent Lightning v1.0, a compact framework for training agents with RL on real harnesses.

item.title: Multimodal open d1 decision models for the edge
item.description: Hugging Face blog on open multimodal decision models sized for edge devices.

item.title: Google’s new SynthID website can identify AI-generated media
item.description: TechCrunch covers Google's new SynthID site for identifying AI-generated media.
